text:
[LCYC.3.1.1] An SCC of the rule graph is admitted despite [LCYC.3.1]
when both hold: no schema is both emitted by a rule of the SCC and
matched, positively or under `no`, by a rule of the SCC; and the SCC
consumes nothing its rules produce through a `call` or the cache, and
no rule of the SCC matches, via `latest` or `then`, a schema a rule of
the SCC emits. Every internal edge of an admitted SCC is then a
`withdraw` edge under [LCYC.3.2.2].

The SCC consumes what a `call` produces when a rule of it carries the
`call` and a rule of it has a pattern, positively or under `no`, over the
service's response schema or over `CallError`; for a service declared with
no response, over `CallError` alone ([LCRS.17.1]). The SCC consumes what
the cache holds when a rule of it carries a `cache` or `cache_delete` of a
key and a rule of it reads `cached()`, in a `where` or a `let`, on that
key ([LSTO.4.3.1b]). A key that is not a literal is the same key as
every other. A `call` or a cache write whose product no rule of the SCC
consumes does not stop the SCC being admitted.

An admitted program stands on one of two grounds, decided by the rule graph
before [LCYC.6.1] drops any edge. A program whose
every SCC of that graph meets the conditions above stands on the
stratification they describe: no SCC emits a schema it matches, so a firing
cannot re-enter its own SCC whatever values it emits. A program that meets
them only after [LCYC.6.1] has dropped an edge stands on the break's ground:
each dropped edge joins an emit to a pattern whose literal test the emitted
literal fails ([LCYC.6.1.2]), so the firing creates no activation across that
edge, and the SCCs that remain meet the conditions above. The first ground
does not read values; the second reads the literal comparison [LCYC.6.1.2]
defines, and holds exactly as far as that comparison is by value.

alloy.name: iret_12_2__admitted_support_acyclic
alloy.note: Condition (a) of this clause -- no kind both emitted and matched within one SCC -- makes fact-level support acyclic: the consequence [IRET.12.2] states and the count's correctness rests on, derived from the condition alone. The direct statement at scope 4; at scope 6 through `lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_kind_graph_acyclic` and `rarc_5_6_6__derives_projects_onto_kinds`, which compose into it. Conditions (b) and (c) take no part.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__admitted
alloy.note: Condition (a) alone, over the emit-edge graph: no kind both emitted by a rule of an SCC and matched, positively or under `no`, by a rule of the same SCC. Conditions (b) (`call`, `cache`, `cache_delete`) and (c) (`latest`, `then`) are not drawn. The compiler's SCCs are the drawn graph's, `lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_graph`.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_graph
alloy.note: Condition (a) over the SCCs of the drawn graph, emit and withdraw edges together -- the SCCs `dsc.cycle` takes, as its `lcyc_3_1_1_admitted` tests condition (a) over schemas. Conditions (b) and (c) are not drawn, and neither are the call and cache edge forms.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_graph_implies_admitted
alloy.note: The admission over the compiler's SCCs implies the admission over the emit-edge SCCs, at scope 6: withdraw edges only coarsen the SCCs. So `iret_12_2__admitted_support_acyclic` and `lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_kind_graph_acyclic` hold of every program the compiler admits over emit and withdraw edges; for the call and cache forms the same holds by the same argument, undrawn.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__admitted_kind_graph_acyclic
alloy.note: Under condition (a) the kind graph -- k1 -> k2 when some rule matches k1 and emits k2 -- is acyclic, at scope 6: a kind cycle names rules that share an SCC and a kind emitted and matched inside it. The rules-and-kinds half of the support-acyclicity argument.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__internal_edges_are_withdraw
alloy.note: The clause's last sentence, at scope 6: under the admission over the compiler's SCCs, every edge inside an SCC is a withdraw edge -- an internal emit edge is a kind emitted by one rule of the SCC and read by another, which condition (a) forbids. TEETH: an admission testing 'emitted twice' instead of 'emitted and read' admits a two-rule emit cycle over two kinds, and the check fails with it.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__same_scc
alloy.note: Two rules of one SCC: each reaches the other through the emit edges, or they are one rule.

alloy.name: lcyc_3_1_1__same_scc_graph
alloy.note: Two rules of one SCC of the drawn graph, the compiler's: each reaches the other through emit or withdraw edges, or they are one rule.

idris.name: Lcyc_3_1_1__cert_emit
idris.note: Models the GENERAL condition (a) including the recursion exception (a `logical`, key-all-slots relation may be emitted-and-read if not withdrawn in the same stratum). This clause requires no emitted-and-read kind to exist in the SCC at all; every program it admits satisfies this predicate vacuously (the antecedent never holds), but the reverse does not hold. Proven for more than the clause states, not less -- the AbsentTrichotomy.idr shape of `partial`.

idris.name: Lcyc_3_1_1__certified
idris.note: Bundles cert_emit, range and the stratification/range-restriction fields into one certificate. Same gap as cert_emit: admits the recursive case this clause refuses.

idris.name: Lcyc_3_1_1__range
idris.note: The range-restriction condition (b): every emitted value is a program literal or a copy of a bound fact's value. Unconditional -- no recursion exception here -- so this half of the certificate is not narrower than what this clause admits.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain
idris.note: The witness program: two rules in two strata, the second reading what the first emits. No stratum reads a kind it emits, which is the clause's condition with one stratum per SCC.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_guard
idris.note: The witness program's guard: every match is admitted.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_is_certified
idris.note: The core certificate inhabited by the same program, through the projection from the certificate with truth maintenance.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_is_certified_tms
idris.note: THE CERTIFICATE IS INHABITED by a program with two strata and an emit a later stratum reads. The hypothesis of the termination theorem with truth maintenance, and of the theorems that rank support, is met by a program that does something. One program: no claim that the certificate admits every program the clause admits.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_life
idris.note: Every kind of the witness program is a `logical` relation.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_no_emit_read
idris.note: No stratum of the witness program reads a kind it emits: the clause's condition, checked stratum by stratum.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_r0
idris.note: Rule 0 of the witness program: matches kind 0, emits kind 1.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_r1
idris.note: Rule 1 of the witness program: matches kind 1, the kind rule 0 emits, and emits kind 2.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_range
idris.note: Every value the witness program emits is its one literal: the range restriction.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__chain_val
idris.note: The witness program's one emitted value, a literal.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emit_value
idris.note: Two equal emits carry one value function: a step of the witness's range field.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__one_is_not_zero
idris.note: A kind that is 1 is not 0: a step of the witness's fields.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__only_member
idris.note: The one member of a one-element list: a step of the witness's range field.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__two_is_not_one
idris.note: A kind that is 2 is not 1: a step of the witness's fields.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emit_in_dom
idris.note: The emitted value lands in the domain: a literal, or a copy of a bound value, by the certificate's range. Stated over a range on the domain itself; both engines (Lcyc/Termination.idr's action step, Rete/TmsRun.idr's) call it through `lcyc_3_1_1__range_widen`.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emitted_not_withdrawn
idris.note: A kind emitted and read in one stratum is not withdrawn there, read off `certEmit`. `partial` as `Lcyc_3_1_1__cert_emit` is: the clause admits no emitted-and-read kind, so for every program it admits this lemma's antecedent never holds; it is live only for the recursive exception the clause refuses.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__range_widen
idris.note: A range over some literals is a range over any superset.

idris.name: Lcyc_3_1_1__certified_tms
idris.note: THE CERTIFICATE AT KIND LEVEL: a stratification respecting every kind-level edge in which no kind emitted by a stratum is read by that stratum, and the range restriction. With one stratum per SCC of the KIND graph this is the clause's condition (a) -- no schema both emitted and matched within an SCC. `partial`: the clause's SCCs are those of the graph [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has pruned, so a program admitted only by the break (`compiler/LCYC.6.1_self_edge_kind_flip_ok`) keeps a kind-level edge inside an SCC and has no certificate here; conditions (b) and (c) are not modelled.

idris.name: Lcyc_3_1_1__fire_measure
idris.note: What the termination argument carries through a firing: the core's progress relative to the post-pop state, that rows of strata below the firing one are live, and the kinds of the rows' targets.

idris.name: lcyc_1_1__certified_terminates_tms
idris.note: The termination theorem for this clause's certificate at kind level, on the engine with truth maintenance, for positive programs and inputs with unique ids. `partial`: a program this clause admits only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has no kind-level certificate, and the theorem does not reach it.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__action_measure
idris.note: One action with truth maintenance keeps the firing invariant and the measure data: the core action by the core's progress lemma, the record by the emitted kind, the cascade by `lcyc_3_1_1__cascade_measure`.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__actions_measure
idris.note: The whole RHS keeps the firing invariant and the measure data.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__cascade_measure
idris.note: The whole cascade: the bridge's fixpoint, the tracked activation, and the measure data for the rows the cascade keeps.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__own_reads_none
idris.note: The firing stratum reads no kind emitted at or above it: a reader at i of a kind emitted at i or above puts the emitter at i, which the certificate forbids.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__phase_kinds
idris.note: THE FORWARD-REACHABILITY LEMMA. During a firing at stratum i, a cascade phase retracts only facts of kinds emitted at stratum i or above: a retracted fact is the live target of a row whose activation is dead, that row's rule is not below i since rows below i are live, and the fact's kind is one that rule emits. So the phase is a frame for every stratum at or below i.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__phase_measure
idris.note: One cascade phase keeps the measure data.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__phase_n_measure
idris.note: And so does any number of phases, alongside the cascade invariant and the tracked activation.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__retract_measure
idris.note: A retraction phase keeps the measure data: the components of every stratum at or below the firing one are unchanged, rows below stay live, and targets keep their kinds.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__tms_to_core
idris.note: This clause's certificate is Lcyc/Certificate.idr's certificate: its recursion disjunct is vacuous, so the core's measure and progress lemmas apply unchanged.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__join_wave_rel_halts
idris.note: The join wave, an SCC this clause refuses (X is emitted by one rule and matched by three inside it), quiesces after six firings under the reference source order: three no-op re-emits, three withdrawals. The certificate is conservative here, knowingly -- the clause refuses the emitted-and-matched case without exception. A 720-order REPL sweep (lcyc_3_1_1__sweep_join_wave) found every order quiescent; that run is not a proof.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__row2_diverges
idris.note: An SCC this clause refuses (W emitted by two rules and matched by a third inside it) diverges: after the consumption fires the state recurs with period twelve. The refusal is not gratuitous. Twelve single-firing Refls chained by lcyc_1_1__periodic_diverges.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emit_copy
idris.note: Emit copying the bound fact's payload; B's action in the row-2 SCC.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emit_flip
idris.note: Emit flipping the bound fact's payload; C's action in the row-2 SCC, so every emit around the B <-> C loop is a replace.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__join_wave
idris.note: The join-wave program over a rule order and a lifecycle for every kind.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__join_wave_input
idris.note: One X, one Y, one Z: the join wave's input working memory.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__join_wave_rel
idris.note: The join wave over dedup'd (Relation) kinds in the reference source order; the instance WitnessProofs runs to quiescence.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__join_wave_rules
idris.note: The six rules of the join wave in a fixed reference order; a source order is a permutation of this list.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__perms
idris.note: All permutations of a list; the 720 source orders of the join wave. REPL helper for the sweep.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__row2_prog
idris.note: The three-rule SCC this clause refuses: A consumes X and Y and emits W, B copies W to V, C flips V back to W and emits Y. W and V Entity, Y Relation.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__row2_s0
idris.note: The row-2 SCC's initial state: one X and one Y, propagated.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_a
idris.note: Row-2 SCC rule A: X x, Y y -> withdraw x, emit W. The consumption.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_b
idris.note: Row-2 SCC rule B: W w -> emit V (copy).

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_c
idris.note: Row-2 SCC rule C: V v -> emit W (flip), emit Y. Y closes C -> A.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_rx
idris.note: Join wave RX: Y y, Z z -> emit X. The join whose constituents are each withdrawn and re-emitted.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_ry
idris.note: Join wave RY: X x -> emit Y.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__rule_rz
idris.note: Join wave RZ: X x -> emit Z.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__sweep_join_wave
idris.note: How many of the join wave's 720 source orders fail to quiesce within the fuel, and the first few that do. A REPL sweep, executed rather than proved; every order quiesced within 30.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__wdr
idris.note: Join wave W-rules: K k -> withdraw k, for each of X, Y, Z.

idris.name: lfst_9_2_1__canonical_from_input
idris.note: A positive program certified at kind level as this clause admits it replays every canonical stream from every input with unique ids, every pump quiescent. `partial`: a program admitted only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has no kind-level certificate.

idris.name: iret_12_3__certified_ranked
idris.note: Every run of a program certified at kind level has acyclic support: the table is ranked at every state between actions. What the count's correctness rests on -- no admitted program reaches the difference between the refcount and [LLOG.2.5] -- proved on the engine rather than argued, for the kind-level certificate. `partial`: a program this clause admits only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has no such certificate, and the ranking by a kind's level does not reach it.

idris.name: lcyc_3_1_1__emit_below_read
idris.note: Under the certificate an emitter of a kind sits in a strictly lower stratum than any reader of it: no lower by edge monotonicity, and not the same, since no stratum reads what it emits.

idris.name: iret_12__run_inv_certified
idris.note: The run invariant holds along every run of a positive program certified at kind level, on an input with unique ids: the certificate's domain and range are what the core invariant needs. `partial`: a program this clause admits only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has no kind-level certificate.
